answer: I'd like to talk about something I pick up every single morning before I leave home. An object I genuinely use every single day is my backpack, which has become an essential part of my routine. It's a plain black one made of tough, water-resistant material, which is very handy during the monsoon. It carries everything I need for the day, from my laptop and documents to my water bottle and other essentials. What makes it so useful is how practical and well-organised it is, with plenty of compartments. I keep students' files in the main section, my laptop in a padded sleeve, and small things like keys, pens and a charger in the front pocket, so I never waste time searching for anything. It is comfortable to carry even when heavily loaded, which is genuinely [[invaluable]] during long commutes. I have had it for several years now, and it has proved remarkably [[durable]] despite constant use. My elder sister gave it to me when I started my final year at university, so it has been with me through exams, job interviews and my first years at the consultancy. Honestly, I rely on it so much that I would feel completely lost without it. It might seem like an ordinary object, but it plays a surprisingly important role in keeping my day organised. Over the years it has become a bit worn, but I have grown quite [[attached]] to it. I think it is a perfect example of how the most [[mundane]] objects often turn out to be the most useful ones in daily life.

followUps.q: Would you buy a new backpack soon?
followUps.answer: Not unless it breaks. One of the zips is starting to stick, but I'd rather get it repaired, because it still does its job perfectly and I know exactly where everything goes.

followUps.q: Do you usually carry a lot with you?
followUps.answer: Probably more than I need. Between my laptop, student files, a charger and my water bottle, it gets quite heavy, so I'm trying to [[travel lighter]] and keep more documents digitally.

note: Moved plain-ish mark 'organised' to 'mundane'; reordered so 'how long' follows 'how you use it'; added description, contents, and that his elder sister gave it to him.
